title: Quantized Artifact Evaluation Gate and Canary Rollout
author: Priya Nair
body:
Overview
--------
This document defines the evaluation gate for quantized model artifacts and the associated canary rollout orchestration used by Redwood Inference. It codifies the entry criteria for promoting a quantized artifact from shadow/onboarding environments into production routes (hosted, dedicated, or private), the telemetry and tests required, and the rollback/troubleshooting guidance to tie into existing regression triage playbooks.

Scope
-----
- Applies to artifacts produced by the model onboarding and quantization pipelines (both automatic and manual quant profiles).
- Covers hosted API, Dedicated pools, and Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments where binary/quant artifacts are deployed.
- Integrates with: eval harness, prompt sets and benchmarks, quality guardrails, and regression triage procedures.

Goals and Principles
--------------------
- Safety-first: do not promote artifacts that show statistically significant regressions on prioritized slices.
- Reproducible gating: every promoted artifact must carry provenance (checksums, quant profile, kernel pins).
- Cost- and latency-aware: accept modest throughput/latency regressions only when quality is preserved.
- Fast rollback: automated fallback to pre-quantized or previous-quant artifacts on breach of SLOs.

Acceptance Criteria (high level)
-------------------------------
All of the following must pass for a quantized artifact to be eligible for canary:

- Core prompt-set stability: weighted-regression-delta (WRD) <= 0.03 on the core prompt suite (see Prompt Suite table below).
- Embedding anchor fidelity: mean cosine similarity >= 0.995 on the embedding anchor set.
- Response Stability Index (RSI) >= 0.92 across representative interaction traces.
- Token-level divergence: KL divergence of token distributions <= 0.10 vs float baseline for the same contexts.
- Latency impact: P95 latency <= 1.25x of float baseline for equivalent batch mix.
- Resource footprint: GPU memory footprint and KV-cache size within the profile targets documented in artifact metadata.

Note: Any metric exceeding these thresholds triggers an automated failure and requires an explicit triage (see "Failure Modes").

Detailed Metrics and Thresholds
-------------------------------
- WRD (weighted-regression-delta): aggregated per-slice; slices are weighted by production traffic share. Threshold: 0.03.
- Embedding Cosine: measured on N=2k anchor pairs covering English/Spanish/FR. Threshold: 0.995.
- RSI (Response Stability Index): similarity of canonical answers measured by BLEU+semantic-similarity heuristics; threshold 0.92.
- Token KL: base-10 log KL aggregated over tokens emitted for core prompts; threshold 0.10.
- Latency P95: measured on synthetic & shadow traffic; threshold 1.25x.
- Throughput (tokens/sec/GPU): should not degrade more than 20% for same batch configuration.

Evaluation Pipeline (steps executed by rwi-eval harness)
------------------------------------------------------
1) Artifact registration
   - Upload artifact bundle to artifact storage and record metadata: model_id, model_version, quant_profile_id, checksum (sha256), source-float-checksum, kernel_pins, expected_sequence_length, supported-clients.
   - Example metadata table (see Appendix).

2) Smoke tests (automated, ~15 minutes)
   - Run unit-level generation tests (sanity responses, tokenization roundtrips).
   - Run embedding consistency sanity check on a 200-item anchor subset.
   - Command: rwi-eval smoke --artifact s3://rwi-artifacts/<id> --profile quant 

3) Full harness run (automated, parallelized, 2–6 hours depending on artifact size)
   - Execute core prompt-set, edge-case probes, multilingual anchors, and latency-quality slices.
   - Produce JSON report, per-slice diffs, and a signed acceptance artifact.
   - Command: rwi-eval run --artifact s3://rwi-artifacts/<id> --slices core,edge,multi --profile quant --output report.json

4) Telemetry snapshot
   - Snapshot baseline telemetry from the float baseline run that produced the artifact. Required fields: baseline_tokens_per_sec, baseline_P95_latency_ms, baseline_RSI, baseline_embeddings_stats.json.

5) Signoff gating
   - Automated pass/fail decision based on thresholds above.
   - If pass: artifact moves to "canary-ready" state and a canary deployment is scheduled.
   - If fail: record fail reason, notify model-owner and QE, and open a triage ticket with labels: quant-fail, artifact:<id>.

Canary Rollout Orchestration
----------------------------
Principles: incremental traffic, real-world telemetry, and short feedback loops. Canary uses the same route-level instrumentation as production (token-level, cost, latency, error breakdowns).

Canary configuration (example YAML):

---
canary_name: quant-canary-<model_id>-v<version>
initial_traffic_percent: 2
stages:
  - { percent: 2, duration_hours: 6 }
  - { percent: 10, duration_hours: 24 }
  - { percent: 30, duration_hours: 24 }
monitoring: [rsi, wrd, p95_latency, error_rate, embedding_drift]
rollback_policy:
  breach_thresholds:
    rsi_drop_absolute: 0.04
    wrd_increase_absolute: 0.02
    p95_ratio: 1.5
    error_rate_absolute: 0.01
  immediate_on_breach: true
---

Traffic routing is controlled by the canary controller (service: canary-orch) which will bump percentages according to the YAML schedule if and only if monitoring windows show no threshold breach. Canary controller posts events to #canary-observability and creates an automated incident if immediate_on_breach triggers.

Promotion checklist (pre-rollout)
--------------------------------
- [ ] Artifact metadata published and signed.
- [ ] Eval harness report uploaded and signed.
- [ ] QE and model owner sign off on per-slice notes (explicitly mark tolerated regressions).
- [ ] Canary YAML created and reviewed by infra and SRE on-call.
- [ ] Backup fallback (previous float artifact or previous quant artifact) staged and smoke-tested.

Failure Modes and Triage Guidance
--------------------------------
Common failure categories and immediate checks: 
- Tokenization / vocabulary drift
  - Symptom: high token KL and degraded RSI on short prompts.
  - First-check: verify tokenizer version and tokenization parity with float baseline.
- Kernel mismatch / pinned-kernel divergence
  - Symptom: large latency variance, small but systematic generation differences on long context.
  - First-check: confirm kernel_pins listed in artifact metadata are available and identical on target fleet.
- Quant rounding and clipping
  - Symptom: semantic shift in numeric outputs, embedding drift on numeric-heavy prompts.
  - First-check: run the per-token delta diagnostic in rwi-eval with --debug-quant to produce token-level rounding stats.
- Cache/KV interaction issues
  - Symptom: failures or degraded quality after repeated multi-turns.
  - First-check: run a kv-cache stress scenario from the harness (rwi-eval kv-stress).

Linking to Regression Triage
---------------------------
When a canary breach occurs, the canary controller automatically creates a triage ticket (component: applied-ml/regression) and attaches: the full rwi-eval report, canary telemetry snapshots, and the artifact metadata. Use the regression-triage playbooks to run bisect, blame-assistant, and probe-farm if needed. Prioritize triage steps that can rule out infra/kernel mismatches before assuming a model-quality regression.

Ownership and Contacts
----------------------
- Model owner: defined on artifact metadata (required).
- QE contact: applied-ml-qe@redwood.example.com.
- Canary controller / infra owner: infra-orch@redwood.example.com.
- On-call SRE (short link): /eng-sre/oncall-rotations/current

Appendix A — Artifact metadata table (required fields)
------------------------------------------------------
| field                    | description                                                  | example                       | required |
|-------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------|----------|
| model_id                | internal canonical model id                                  | rwi-llama-65b                 | yes      |
| model_version           | semantic version or build id                                 | v2026-02-10-quant             | yes      |
| quant_profile_id        | id of quantization profile used                               | qprof-int8-kv-opt-v2          | yes      |
| sha256_checksum         | artifact bundle checksum                                      | 9f3b...a12c                   | yes      |
| float_source_checksum   | checksum of float baseline artifact                           | 1a2b...9f8c                   | yes      |
| kernel_pins             | list of GPU kernel ABI tags expected                           | [cu12-kern-v3, cu11-kern-v9]  | yes      |
| expected_seq_len        | expected typical sequence length                              | 1024                          | recommended |
| memory_footprint_mb     | expected GPU memory usage for profile                          | 34567                         | recommended |
| provenance_uri          | S3 or internal URI for build logs and reproducibility manifest | s3://rwi-builds/1234/manifest | yes      |

Appendix B — Example triage commands
------------------------------------
- Run full eval harness locally: rwi-eval run --artifact s3://rwi-artifacts/<id> --slices core,edge,multi --output /tmp/report.json
- Run per-token quant debug: rwi-eval debug-quant --artifact <id> --prompt-file core-prompts.txt --out quant-debug.csv
- Trigger a controlled canary rollback: rwi-canary rollback --canary quant-canary-<id> --reason "p95 breach" --initiator <username>

Notes and Caveats
------------------
- This gate is tuned for production safety. Teams may create experimental quant profiles that bypass parts of the gate for research, but such artifacts must be explicitly labeled "experimental" and are not eligible for any production routing.
- Some customers (private on-prem) will have custom kernel availability; ensure kernel_pins and artifact packaging are validated in the customer's staging cluster before promotion.
